answer: A zephyr of new identities is cheap, so an agent economy can make each identity carry a slowly grown, verifiable work history — a lotus that only opens after sustained honest service. Every agent signs its contributions with a single persistent quill, a key whose reputation is earned over time and cannot be transferred; creating ten fresh identities buys ten empty histories. An attacker must then pay the full time and effort cost for each fake, while honest agents keep the trust they built, so Sybil attacks stop scaling.
